neighbors.title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
neighbors.abstract: In this study, we investigate whether attention-based information flow inside large language models (LLMs) is aggregated through noticeable patterns for long context processing. Our observations reveal that LLMs aggregate information through Pyramidal Information Funneling where attention is scattering widely in lower layers, progressively consolidating within specific contexts, and ultimately focusing on critical tokens (a.k.a massive activation or attention sink) in higher layers. Motivated by these insights, we developed PyramidKV, a novel and effective KV cache compression method. neighbors.title: KV Cache Compression for Inference Efficiency in LLMs: A Review

neighbors.title: GPU Efficiency Without Compromise: LLM Inference Optimization Through Dynamic Batching, KV-Cache Management, and Intelligent Scheduling
neighbors.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) inference at scale faces critical bottlenecks in GPU utilization, latency, and cost-per-token that threaten the economic viability of production AI deployments. This paper presents a comprehensive optimization framework for production LLM inference systems, integrating four synergistic techniques: phase-aware scheduling, dynamic batching, multi-tier KV-cache memory optimization, and quantization techniques. Through rigorous analysis of production deployments, we demonstrate that organizations can achieve 3-10x improvements in throughput while reducing inference costs by 30-50% without sacrificing output quality.

Despite this need, there lacks an efficient solution for offloading and transferring KV caches. neighbors.title: Multi-Token Attention

neighbors.title: Efficient LLM Inference with Kcache
neighbors.abstract: Large Language Models(LLMs) have had a profound impact on AI applications, particularly in the domains of long-text comprehension and generation. KV Cache technology is one of the most widely used techniques in the industry. It ensures efficient sequence generation by caching previously computed KV states. However, it also introduces significant memory overhead. We discovered that KV Cache is not necessary and proposed a novel KCache technique to alleviate the memory bottleneck issue during the LLMs inference process. KCache can be used directly for inference without any training process, Our evaluations show that KCache improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 40% with the baseline, while keeping accuracy.

neighbors.title: Reducing Data Transfer Overhead with CXL-Based Near-Data Processing for LLM Inference
neighbors.abstract: In Large Language Models (LLMs), the Key-Value (KV) cache demands a substantial memory footprint as the input sequence length grows. In this paper, we offload the KV cache to Compute Express Link (CXL) memory and leverage Near-Data Processing (NDP) to select and transfer only the KV cache entries that highly affect model accuracy. Our approach reduces the data transfer overhead caused by limited CXL bandwidth and achieves an average 1.45× speedup over the baseline GPU with CXL memory.

neighbors.title: On power and performance tradeoff of L2 cache compression
neighbors.abstract: This paper presents the power-performance trade off of three different cache compression algorithms. Cache compression improves performance, since the compressed data increases the effective cache capacity by reducing the cache misses. The unused memory cells can be put into sleep mode to save static power. The increased performance and saved power due to cache compression must be more than the delay and power consumption added due to CODEC(COmpressor and DECompressor) block respectively. Among the studied algorithms, powerdelay characteristic of Frequent Pattern compression(FPC) is found to be the most suitable for cache compression.
